h.strategy: Favor hypotheses driven by strong structural mechanisms: (1) an edit matters less when the part it modifies is disconnected, bypassed, or redundant in the parent; (2) diminishing returns: adding capacity helps less when the parent already has plenty, and removing it hurts more when the parent has little; (3) bottlenecks: improving a component helps more when it is the sole path or limiting factor. Prefer conditions that change the edit's effect by a large amount over subtle ones. Avoid hypotheses whose direction depends on fine balances between competing effects. State each hypothesis's mechanism in one sentence.

hyps.why: With node 1 cut off from the input, a conv on edge 1->2 carries no signal and gains nothing.
With node 1 disconnected, a conv on edge 1->3 is dead and adds no benefit.
If edge 5 is removed, node 2 cannot reach the output, so upgrading edge 2 is irrelevant.
Edge 1 only feeds node 2, which is dead when edge 5 is absent, so the conv is wasted.
Adding a conv to an empty direct edge gains more than replacing an existing op.
Filling an empty edge into the output adds a new path, unlike a swap.
Filling an empty edge adds a new route to the output, beating a replacement gain.
Setting an already-none edge to none is a no-op, whereas removing an existing op usually hurts.
Removing an already-absent edge is a no-op, whereas removing a live edge usually hurts.
Removing edge 2 is a no-op when node 1 is disconnected but costs accuracy otherwise.
